claims.text: Systematically varying noble-metal composition during synthesis promotes formation of a uniform single-phase high-entropy alloy nanomaterial.
Systematic composition variation produces an optimized, homogeneous atomic distribution.
A uniform single-phase structure with optimized atomic distribution enhances catalytic performance relative to conventional monometallic catalysts.
An optimal elemental composition promotes entropic stabilization of the alloy.
An optimal elemental composition minimizes lattice-strain heterogeneity.
Reduced lattice-strain heterogeneity and entropic stabilization support structural uniformity.
Structural uniformity modulates the electronic properties, including d-band characteristics, of surface atoms.
The proposed modulation of surface electronic properties reduces catalytic activation barriers.
An optimized composition will increase catalytic reaction rates relative to a monometallic or non-optimized catalyst.
An optimized composition will improve catalytic selectivity relative to a monometallic or non-optimized catalyst.

The proposed relationship is limited to noble-metal-based high-entropy alloys synthesized under conditions favoring single-phase formation and within composition ranges supporting entropic stabilization.
X-ray diffraction can be used to evaluate phase purity and crystallinity in the controlled comparison.
Electron microscopy can be used to evaluate atomic distribution in the controlled comparison.
